records.name: Ben Nevis
records.description: The highest mountain in the United Kingdom, drawing walkers from around the world for its summit views, history, and challenging weather.

records.name: Glen Nevis
records.description: Beautiful glen beneath Ben Nevis with dramatic mountain walls, forested lower slopes, and easy access to major hiking routes.
records.address: Glen Nevis, Fort William PH33 6SY, Scotland

records.name: Ben Nevis Visitor Centre
records.description: Main information and trailhead hub for the Mountain Track, helping visitors prepare for climbs on Ben Nevis.
records.address: Glen Nevis, Fort William PH33 6ST, Scotland

records.name: Steall Falls
records.description: One of Scotland's highest waterfalls, reached by a famously scenic walk through the upper end of Glen Nevis.
records.address: Upper Glen Nevis, Fort William PH33 6SY, Scotland

records.name: Nevis Range Mountain Resort
records.description: All-season outdoor resort offering gondola access, mountain biking, winter sports, and wide-ranging views over Lochaber.

records.name: Nevis Range Gondola
records.description: Mountain gondola rising the north side of Aonach Mòr and opening up panoramic Highland viewpoints with minimal effort.

records.name: Aonach Mòr
records.description: High Munro above Fort William known for broad summit plateaux, ski terrain, and dramatic outlooks over Lochaber.

records.name: West Highland Museum
records.description: Town museum telling the story of Lochaber through Jacobite, archaeological, military, and social history collections.
records.address: Cameron Square, Fort William PH33 6AJ, Scotland

records.name: Old Inverlochy Castle
records.description: Impressive 13th-century ruin beside the River Lochy, among the most complete medieval castles left in mainland Scotland.

records.name: Neptune's Staircase
records.description: Spectacular flight of canal locks on the Caledonian Canal, regarded as one of Thomas Telford's great engineering works.

records.name: Caledonian Canal at Banavie
records.description: Busy canal-side stretch where boats, towpaths, swing bridges, and mountain views create one of Lochaber's most recognisable scenes.

records.name: Jacobite Steam Train
records.description: Famous steam-hauled rail journey from Fort William to Mallaig, celebrated for crossing the Glenfinnan Viaduct.
records.address: Fort William railway station, Fort William PH33 6EN, Scotland

records.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct
records.description: Iconic concrete railway viaduct curving above Glenfinnan, with commanding views over Loch Shiel and Highland hills.

records.name: Glenfinnan Monument
records.description: Towering column marking the start of the 1745 Jacobite rising beside the head of Loch Shiel.

records.name: Glenfinnan Station Museum
records.description: Small railway museum and station complex overlooking the viaduct, combining transport history with classic Highland scenery.

records.name: Commando Memorial
records.description: Moving memorial to the British Commandos, set on a hill with a sweeping view toward Ben Nevis and the Nevis Range.

records.name: Spean Bridge Viewpoint
records.description: Highland village viewpoint area popular as a stop on the way north from Fort William, especially for mountain panoramas.

records.name: Loch Linnhe Shore
records.description: Sea loch shoreline beside Fort William where visitors can enjoy waterfront walks and views south toward Ardgour.

records.name: Corpach Shipwreck Viewpoint
records.description: Well-known photo stop looking across Loch Linnhe to the wreck of a small vessel with Ben Nevis often rising behind.

records.name: Lochaber Geopark Gateway
records.description: Gateway point for exploring a geopark famed for volcanoes, glaciers, mountain-building, and some of Britain's biggest landscapes.

records.name: West Highland Way Terminus
records.description: Northern end of Scotland's best-known long-distance trail, marked in the centre of Fort William after the full route from Milngavie.
records.address: Gordon Square, Fort William PH33 6DY, Scotland

records.name: Great Glen Way
records.description: Long-distance route linking Fort William with Inverness through the Great Glen, following lochs, canal sections, and forest tracks.

records.name: Ben Nevis Distillery
records.description: Traditional whisky distillery founded in the 19th century and closely associated with Fort William's industrial past.
records.address: Lochy Bridge, Fort William PH33 6TJ, Scotland

records.name: Glen Coe
records.description: One of Scotland's most dramatic glens, famed for volcanic scenery, towering peaks, and deep historical resonance.

records.name: Three Sisters of Glen Coe
records.description: Classic roadside viewpoint onto three steep ridges descending from Bidean nam Bian, among the most photographed Highland scenes.

records.name: Buachaille Etive Mòr
records.description: Iconic pyramid-shaped mountain standing guard at the entrance to Glen Coe, beloved by walkers and photographers.

records.name: Glencoe Visitor Centre
records.description: National Trust for Scotland visitor centre interpreting the glen's geology, ecology, and the story of the 1692 massacre.

records.name: Glencoe Mountain Resort
records.description: Mountain centre offering skiing, hill access, and dramatic viewpoints on the high pass east of Glen Coe.

records.name: Loch Achtriochtan
records.description: Photogenic loch lying directly beneath the great walls of the Three Sisters and surrounding peaks.

records.name: Signal Rock
records.description: Woodland site associated in local tradition with the 1692 Massacre of Glencoe and valued for short walks and atmosphere.

records.name: Lost Valley
records.description: Hidden hanging valley once used for sheltering cattle, reached by an adventurous walk from the base of the Three Sisters.

records.name: Fort William High Street and Old Fort Area
records.description: Compact town-centre area that anchors Fort William's role as the outdoor capital of Lochaber.
records.address: High Street, Fort William PH33 6DH, Scotland

records.name: Old Fort Site
records.description: Site recalling the original government fort from which Fort William took its name.
records.address: Loch Linnhe waterfront, Fort William PH33 6DB, Scotland

records.name: Cow Hill
records.description: Popular short hillwalk above town delivering expansive views across Loch Linnhe, Glen Nevis, and Fort William.
records.address: Near Lundavra Road, Fort William PH33 6RF, Scotland

records.name: Ardnamurchan Point
records.description: Remote and windswept western extremity of mainland Britain, prized for sea views, wildlife, and a real edge-of-the-map feel.

records.name: Ardnamurchan Lighthouse
records.description: 19th-century lighthouse dramatically perched above cliffs at the far western tip of the Ardnamurchan peninsula.

records.name: Mallaig Harbour
records.description: Working west coast harbour and end point for the famous rail journey from Fort William, with ferries and sea views toward the Small Isles.

records.name: Loch Eil
records.description: Long sea loch west of Fort William edged by woodland, scattered settlements, and scenic road and rail approaches.
records.address: Loch Eil, near Fort William, Scotland

records.name: Mamores Viewpoint
records.description: Viewpoint area toward the Mamores ridge, famous for serrated summits rising south of Glen Nevis.
records.address: Glen Nevis, Fort William PH33 6SY, Scotland

records.name: Banavie Swing Bridge
records.description: Canal crossing near Neptune's Staircase where boats, trains, and mountain backdrops come together in one classic Lochaber scene.
